slot.brief: Given molality and observed vs theoretical freezing point depression, compute van 't Hoff factor and infer association/dissociation.

stem: A $0.10\ \text{m}$ solution of a solute in benzene shows a freezing point depression of $0.256\ \text{K}$. Given $K_\text{f} = 5.12\ \text{K kg mol}^{-1}$ for benzene, the van 't Hoff factor ($i$) and the state of the solute in the solution are:

verdicts.working: i = ΔTf/(Kf·m) = 0.256/(5.12×0.10) = 0.50. i < 1 indicates association; complete dimerization gives i = 1/2 = 0.50, consistent.

working:
1. Calculate the theoretical (normal) freezing point depression assuming no association or dissociation:
$$\Delta T_{\text{f, theoretical}} = K_\text{f} \cdot m = 5.12\ \text{K kg mol}^{-1} \times 0.10\ \text{mol kg}^{-1} = 0.512\ \text{K}$$

2. Compute the van 't Hoff factor ($i$):
$$i = \dfrac{\Delta T_{\text{f, observed}}}{\Delta T_{\text{f, theoretical}}} = \dfrac{0.256\ \text{K}}{0.512\ \text{K}} = 0.50$$

3. Infer the state of the solute:
Since $i < 1$, the solute undergoes association. For complete dimerization ($2\text{A} \rightarrow \text{A}_2$):
$$i = 1 - \alpha\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{n}\right) = 1 - 1\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 0.50$$
Thus, the solute undergoes complete dimerization.

Independent check: i = ΔTf/(Kf·m) = 0.256/(5.12×0.10) = 0.50. i < 1 indicates association; complete dimerization gives i = 1/2 = 0.50, consistent.

C: Takes the reciprocal ratio $i = \Delta T_\text{theoretical} / \Delta T_\text{observed} = 2.00$, and mistakenly thinks a factor of 2 indicates dimerization.
